findings.claim: Observed on macOS (darwin), Node 24.2.0 and npm 11.3.0, in a 0700 scratch copy made with git archive of 8543f338, with the private overlay copied over the starter. A learner whose form is correct by the module's own teaching can have a correct Task 8 test rejected, with messages that send them to add checks they already have. The accessible-forms topic (artifact.md objective line 5 and line 42) teaches that a label may be associated through htmlFor and id or by wrapping the control. I changed only the scratch copy of the solved form so that the 'Owning team' label wraps the select instead of using htmlFor. Tests 1-7 and my own complete, README-faithful test 8 still pass (Tests 8 passed (8)). npm test then exits 1 and lists three misses: the form ignoring the blank submission, a blank submission calling onSave, and the form ignoring the completed submission. Those are exactly the three variants that act through the document submit listener. They need readForm to find both fields, and fieldByLabel (lines 9-18) compares the label's raw textContent with the exact caption. A label that wraps a select also contains every option's text, so the team field is never found and the three variants silently do nothing. This cause is reasoned from the code; the outcome was observed. Testing Library's getByLabelText, which test 2 uses, ignores the select's own text, so the public tests accept this markup and the Task 8 check does not. Wrapping only the name input was also probed and is accepted, so the trigger is a label that wraps the select. The starter TASK 2 comment and README task 2 do steer learners to htmlFor and id, which limits how often this happens. When it does happen, the learner cannot fix it by changing their test, and every message points at assertions the test already makes.
findings.recommendation: Find the fields the way the learner's test and test 2 do: by accessible label, ignoring the text of nested form controls (for example, compare the label's text without option, select, input and textarea content, or resolve fields through the form's labelled elements). Alternatively, have the variant fail closed: if it cannot find both fields, report that the check could not read the form and name the labels it expects, rather than counting the variant as not caught. Add a wrapping-label form to the oracle's regression probes.

findings.claim: Observed on macOS (darwin), Node 24.2.0 and npm 11.3.0, in a 0700 scratch copy made with git archive of 8543f338, with the private overlay copied over the starter. The disclosure says one scored check is that onSave receives 'the entered name and team' (README lines 130-133), and the complete-wrong-values message says 'Check the name and team that onSave receives' (verify-learner-test.mjs line 67). Only the name is actually scored. The altered-values variant changes only the name (task8-variant.jsx line 56). A complete test whose only onSave check is that the call contained the entered name was accepted with the Task 8 line. The same test checking only the team was rejected with 'Check the name and team that onSave receives'. The over-claim is small and the message is learner-safe, but the README states a scored check that does not run. lab.json cleanup.notes ('onSave receives the entered values') and the ui-tests topic.json reason are vaguer and not wrong.
findings.recommendation: Either score the team as well, with a second altered-values variant that changes only the team (one variant that changes both fields would still accept a name-only test), or change the README and the message to say that the entered name is scored and the team is self-checked.

findings.claim: Observed on macOS (darwin), Node 24.2.0 and npm 11.3.0, in a 0700 scratch copy made with git archive of 8543f338, with the private overlay copied over the starter. The completion criterion conflicts with the split permission next to it. README task 8 (lines 122-123) says 'You may split the scenario into more than one test'. 'Expected output' (lines 140-142) says 'The run summary must show Test Files  8 passed (8) and Tests  8 passed (8)'. My accepted split test, two tests plus one test.todo, printed 'Tests  9 passed | 1 todo (10)' followed by the Task 8 line, and npm test exited 0. A learner who splits, as invited, sees a summary the README says is wrong, although the lab is complete. The decisive signal, the Task 8 line with exit 0, is correct.
findings.recommendation: Make the Task 8 line and exit code 0 the completion signal. Say that the Tests count is 8 for a single learner test and higher if you split test 8 (Test Files stays 8 passed (8)). Optionally, add the same note to expected/on-completion.txt.

findings.claim: Starter step 5 is hard to read and its matcher hint leads to one avoidable failure. Line 16 is 139 characters long. It joins the end of step 5's matcher sentence and the start of the queryBy note into one run-on line ('...with the name and team). queryBy ... not.toBeInTheDocument() proves an element is'), unlike every other wrapped line in the comment. Observed on macOS (darwin), Node 24.2.0 and npm 11.3.0, in a 0700 scratch copy made with git archive of 8543f338, with the private overlay copied over the starter. Following the hint literally, with toHaveBeenCalledWith given an object of only the name and team, fails the normal test 8 run, because the form also passes notify. The Vitest diff shows the extra 'notify': false, and the ServiceForm comment documents { name, team, notify }, so the learner can recover. Still, the first failure comes from the hint's wording rather than from the form.
findings.recommendation: Reflow lines 13-17 so each step wraps like the rest of the comment. Word the hint as 'with the values the form passes (name, team and notify)', or point to expect.objectContaining({ name, team }).

findings.claim: Step 10 of the loop-3 plan is half done. The module lock was regenerated, but the solved run was not re-recorded. coding-lab-solved-run.json still records the run at 30cd7583 (lines 4-5), with summaries 'Tests 8 passed (8)' and no Task 8 oracle line, and it binds the old README and lab.json hashes. Its toolchain names only darwin, and it does not list Windows as unverified. The loop-3 reconciliation required that statement until a Windows run is recorded, and edu-fcc-t1 recommended it. Learners do not see this file. It matters to the education review because lab.json still declares windows in os, and the only evidence for the redesigned test 8 path is this critic's macOS run and the author's.
findings.recommendation: Re-record the solved run at the reviewed commit, including the Task 8 oracle outcome. Add a note that Windows (and Linux, if not run) parity is reasoned, not observed, until a run is recorded.

Observed on macOS (darwin), Node 24.2.0 and npm 11.3.0, in a 0700 scratch copy made with git archive of 8543f338, with the private overlay copied over the starter. The mutation oracle this finding asked for exists and works: an unchanged control plus five runtime variants of the learner's own form. My README-style complete test, and a stylistically different split, extensionless, regex-named one, are accepted with the Task 8 line. Rejected, each naming the missed behaviours: a vacuous test (render, a TEAMS length check and an onSave-not-called check with no submit), which got all five messages; blank-only; the scenario without any onSave-received check; and an onSave-called check without values. A fireEvent and container test that checks the error and the onSave values is accepted. That matches the disclosure: role and label queries, user-event and query variants are self-checked.

Steps 3 and 5 (lines 10-17) still say findBy for an error that appears, and queryBy with not.toBeInTheDocument for absence, noting that findBy rejects when an element is missing. They name user.type and user.selectOptions. README task 8 (lines 115-123) describes the same query choices, with no conflict. Line 16's formatting and matcher hint are raised separately as edu-fcc-u4.

The coupling note is at README lines 60-63: tests 4-7 build on tasks 1-3, and test 7 also needs the task 6 'Service deleted' toast. Line 111 keeps 'announce "Service deleted"' in the task 6 summary. On the shipped starter, tests 4-7 fail with the task 2 label message, as disclosed.

The file is unchanged since loop 3. Lines 22-32 spy on preventDefault and require a cancelled submit. Observed on the shipped starter at 8543f338: test 3 fails with 'handleSubmit must call event.preventDefault(): expected 0 to be greater than 0'. README troubleshooting (lines 172-173) still maps the jsdom requestSubmit trace to a missing preventDefault.
README lines 31-41 still start the optional block 'from the tests folder', use 'cd ../starter', and say to run tests in a second terminal and stop the server with Ctrl+C.

The verifier runs the normal suite first and exits on its result, adding no new cross-task coupling. Observed: the shipped starter fails all 8 tests under the lab.json failingTests names, and the oracle does not run. The private solution passes 8/8 and prints the Task 8 line, with exit 0.
The labelled assertion is still at lines 29-32. Observed on the shipped starter at 8543f338: '-> handleSubmit must call event.preventDefault(): expected 0 to be greater than 0', which names the fix.

The Windows defects are removed in the code. This is reasoned; not run on Windows. Lines 12-26 spawn process.execPath with node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs (no shell, no .cmd shim), and line 22 prints the spawn error before exiting. vitest.mutation.config.js (lines 25-33) compares normalized forward-slash paths, case-folded on win32, instead of a raw path.resolve result. Results are read from a JSON output file, not from parsed console text. Observed on macOS: the runner works end to end. Windows and Linux parity remain unverified. The solved-run evidence does not say so and was not re-recorded; that is raised as edu-fcc-u5.
